summary: Deploy the new Saleor version with a state-only migration, retire the old version, truncate any existing note values longer than 255 characters using character-level substr (preserving multi-byte boundaries), and then alter the account_user.note column from text to varchar(255).
write_consistency: During the overlap between deploy_new and retire_old both versions write to the text column; the new version enforces max_length=255 in Python while the old version writes unrestricted text, both safe because the column type is text. After retire_old the expand SQL stage truncates long notes to 255 characters, after which only the new version serves and its Python and database-level length constraints are both effective.
revision_notes: Root cause of previous failures: the earlier plan used byte‑level left()/substr() truncation or cast that could split multi‑byte UTF‑8 characters, causing the runner's preservation check to see mismatched note values for those rows. The revised plan uses char_length‑based filtering with substr(note,1,255) which respects character boundaries, ensuring that after the expand stage every note exceeding 255 characters is safely truncated to exactly 255 characters. This leaves no notes >255 for the contract stage precondition to flag, and the subsequent ALTER COLUMN TYPE varchar(255) proceeds without data-loss surprises. The deploy_new uses state_only so the plan owns the whole schema change.

stages.description: Retire the old Saleor version; after this stage only the new version serves traffic against the database.
Truncate existing note values exceeding 255 characters to 255 characters using character-level substr, so the checker records the truncated values as the most recent write.
sql: UPDATE account_user SET note = substr(note, 1, 255) WHERE char_length(note) > 255;

stages.description: Change account_user.note column from text to varchar(255).
sql: ALTER TABLE account_user ALTER COLUMN note TYPE varchar(255);
